faena: He looked out at the bull, planning his faena, his work with the red cloth that was to reduce the bull, to make him manageable.
“The papers said they never saw a better faena,” Manuel said.
faery:
To guard your steps securely up, where streams
A faery moonshine washing pale the crowds
Of pointed stars.  Remember not whereby
Lives of the Duke of Wellington, for example; Spinoza; the works of Dickens; the Faery Queen; a Greek dictionary with the petals of poppies pressed to silk between the pages; all the Elizabethans.

Would be too proud to bend
To sing the faery tunes that brim
My heart from end to end.

Good society has its claret and its velvet carpets, its dinner engagements six weeks deep, its opera, and its faery ball rooms . . . gets its science done by Faraday and its religion by the superior clergy who are to be met in the best houses; how should it have need of belief and emphasis?
